notes:
Context and summary:
- Account: global e-commerce marketplace (2k+ sellers) planning to replace a mix of embeddings + lightweight chat for customer support, product reranking for search, and personalization signals.
- Primary ask: dedicated capacity with firm throughput guarantees to allow them to retire an on-prem cluster and commit to a 12-month reserved spend. Finance needs min tokens/sec to justify price.
Throughput / concurrency requirements (customer asks):
- Minimum sustained throughput asked: 75,000 tokens/sec aggregate across the reserved pool (30-day rolling average).
- Concurrency caps requested: 120 concurrent active chat sessions (interactive), plus 600 concurrent short embedding/rerank requests.
- Max request length constraints: typical requests 256-1,024 tokens; burst events include batched rerank jobs up to 4,096 tokens per call.
- Burst policy requested: allow bursting to 2.0x sustained throughput for up to 10 minutes per hour, and 4.0x for 2 minutes for sale events; BlueHarbor wants these defined in contract.
Redwood responses and recommendations:
- Baseline proposal: reserved pool equivalent to 6x A100-80GB (or 4x H100 equivalent) with autoscale headroom of +2 GPUs for controlled bursts; estimated baseline maps to ~65k tokens/sec sustained for their workload unless model quantization is applied.
- Suggested operational trade-offs: recommend 8-bit quantization on rerank models and caching hot prefixes for chat flows to increase effective tokens/sec without linear GPU add.
- Latency SLOs asked: p95 < 250ms for short prompts, p99 < 900ms; BlueHarbor insists on tighter p95 for customer-facing flows. Redwood counter-offer: p95 < 350ms for sustained workloads at baseline, p95 < 250ms at dedicated higher commit, with automatic fallback to smaller model variants under overload.
SLA negotiation points (open):
- Uptime target: BlueHarbor requests 99.95% for Dedicated; Redwood standard commercial tier is 99.9% — legal to negotiate credits.
- Penalty model: BlueHarbor proposes service credits escrowing up to 15% monthly for repeated misses; Redwood proposed tiered credits (small credit for minor misses, larger for sustained outage) and operational remediation windows.
- Throughput guarantee measurement: dispute over measurement window (customer wants 30-day rolling avg vs Redwood prefers 7-day for burstable metrics). Need explicit metric definition (tokens/sec per pool, tokenization method).
- Concurrency enforcement: customer wants guarantee both at session level and per-request worker caps; Redwood requests ability to route to fallback model variants or region when hitting caps.
POC / pilot plan:
- 2-week pilot on a 4x A100 pool (dedicated) + synthetic replay of Black Friday traffic spike (vendor-supplied trace). Goal: validate sustained tokens/sec, p95/p99 latency, and burst behavior under controlled autoscale.
- Deliverables: perf report with tokens/sec by model variant, tail latency distribution, cost per 1k tokens at baseline and with quantization.
Action items and quotes from customer:
- "We need a hard number for tokens/sec to show procurement — without that finance won't sign." — Head of Infrastructure (R. Alvarez).
- Legal wants explicit definition of outage and a runbook for failover to the private endpoint.
- SE asks: confirm preferred GPU family and whether BlueHarbor will accept model quantization for rerank path.
Next steps:
- Jordan to circulate Redwood's updated pricing + SLA redlines by 2024-12-10.
- Priya to schedule benchmark week (pilot) Jan 6-20 and confirm synthetic trace format.
- Legal teams to exchange draft SLA; BlueHarbor to provide procurement template.
